page.layout: One text column, with marginal notes in the left margin: "Obscura illa Dionys.", "Signa in ædiculâ. Lib.iiii.", "Fixa in terram." and "t.Ann.". Running head above the text. Page number at head. No notes on the right, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.p: lim μακρὸς in Græco, id esset longa) cuius inferior cuspis in acutum definit ut in terram defigi possit, portat. Dico Obscura illa Dionys.intricatum hoc de facello. ubi enim in Numis usquam talis effigies? quin nudæ eæ conspiciuntur (& centenæ aliquot exstant) sine tegmine ullo facelli. Nonne etiam prægraue hoc pondus ferenti fuisset? In columnâ tantum Traiani, nescio quid in alis aquilarum imponitur, quod fateor me non explicare. Nisi ergo Dionis infimo illo ævo mutata aquilæ forma, censeo mentem eius esse, aquilam cum in hibernis esset in facello repositam, atque inde motam cum educenda. Id mihi Herodianus Signa in ædiculâ. Lib.iiii.approbat, qui de Prætorianorum castris loquens, Antoninum venire facit ὡς τὴν νεὼν, ἔνθα τὰ σημεῖα καὶ τὰ ἀγάλ-ματα[?] τῆς στρατιωτικῆς[?] προσκυνεῖται[?]: in facellum, ubi signa & imagines exercitus adorantur. Sed & figulina opera nostra ætate ibi eruta, cum inscriptione, EX AEDICV-LA AVGVSTORVM: quam hanc esse nihil absurdum. Enimuero & olim Romæ signa in templo. Dionysius: Ἐξέλευσεν ἐκ τῶν ἱερῶν τὰ σημεῖα ἐκφέρειν: Iussit è templis signa efferre. Etsi templum verius esset, singulariter: quo-niam reposita ea in erario, templo Saturni. Liuius: Signa Quæstores ex ærario deferre iubet. Et alibi: Signa ærario prompta feruntur ad Dictatorem. Illic igitur, & religionis causâ, & custodiæ, quia pecunia ibi publica & argentum. Nec aliter Galli olim τὰς χρυσᾶς σημαίας τὰς ἀκινήτους λεγομένας ἐν τῷ τῆς Ἀθηνᾶς ἱερῷ εἶχον: aurea signa, quæ Immota vocitabant, in Mineruae templo habebant: quod Polybius scripsit. Est autem in Dionis etiam descriptio-ne, Fixa in terram.defigi in terram solere: quod in exemplis multis legas. Tacitus: t.Ann.Plurimum circa aquilas laborq. quæ neque figi limo-sa humo, neque aduersum ferri ingruentia tela poterant. Fi-gebantur

page.notes: Right margin empty. Doubtful readings: the Greek in the Herodian quotation (ὡς τὴν νεὼν, ἔνθα…, the verb after στρατιωτικῆς) is hard to read at this scan resolution and is marked [?]. The first Greek word μακρὸς is uncertain. "laborq." is printed as shown; it may be "labor quæ" or "laborque" and is kept as printed. "Mineruae" is read with some doubt. The last line "gebantur", set right-aligned, is the continuation of "Fi-" and is kept as text, not as a catchword. The spaced small capitals in "EX AE DIC V-LA AVGVSTORVM" are joined into single words. The note "t.Ann." is read as printed and may be abbreviated differently. The Greek in the Dionysius quotation and the Polybius passage is set in italic in the scan and is copied as seen, with accents.
